about: The transition rows and the three ways a transition is drawn (xfade, expr, process), taken as they were from the original package's boundary file (things-to-store-and-run.json at bitfield-packages commit e16b89fd1f025278be1de62554b0013952d8a7d2, packages/media-composition); a `process` transition runs a script kept beside this file (see stored-bytes.json).

rows.name: xfade
rows.label: Xfade
rows.note: 57 built-in ffmpeg xfade types via `spec`; convenience floor.

rows.name: expr
rows.label: Expr
rows.note: per-pixel custom xfade `expr` (A,B,X,Y,W,H,P); no neighbor sampling.

rows.name: process
rows.label: Process
rows.note: shells ANY binary via `command` template = the unbounded clay renderer (gl-transitions GLSL, RIFE/FILM AI-morph, bespoke).

rows.name: whip-pan
rows.label: Whip pan (motion blur)
rows.note: process renderer; a transition xfade cannot make (sliding motion-blur composite). Proof of clay.

rows.name: luma-fade
rows.label: Luma fade (Kolder matte)
rows.note: Kolder signature luminance-matte reveal (real track-matte, not a blend). Same process slot hosts AI roto (Robust Video Matting/SAM2) by swapping the binary.

rows.name: ai-matte
rows.label: AI object-reveal (RVM roto)
rows.note: AI roto transition (Robust Video Matting): mattes the subject of A (no green screen), holds them while the background crossfades A->B, then fades the subject to full B. The Kolder masking/fly-through move automated. Proof that the process renderer hosts AI transitions with zero engine change.
